 240→# ------------------------------------------------------- the organisers' shape
 241→
 242→
 243→def is_organiser_record(data: Any) -> bool:
 244→    """True for the organisers' shape: a top-level dispute_ticket object."""
 245→    return isinstance(data, dict) and isinstance(data.get("dispute_ticket"), dict)
 246→
 247→
 248→def _object(value: Any) -> Dict[str, Any]:
 249→    return value if isinstance(value, dict) else {}
 250→
 251→
 252→def _copy_present(target: Dict[str, Any], source: Dict[str, Any], key: str, as_key: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
 253→    """Carry a field across under its own name or a renamed one, when it is there.
 254→
 255→    A missing key stays missing rather than becoming an explicit null: the Evidence Pack
 256→    distinguishes "the record does not state this" from "the record states null", and only
 257→    the first is true here.
 258→    """
 259→    value = source.get(key)
 260→    if value is not None:
 261→        target[as_key or key] = value
 262→
 263→
 264→def _event_timestamp(events: Any, event_type: str) -> Optional[str]:
 265→    """The timestamp of the app_events entry of this type, or None if there is no such entry."""
 266→    for event in events if isinstance(events, list) else []:
 267→        if isinstance(event, dict) and event.get("event_type") == event_type:
 268→            timestamp = event.get("timestamp")
 269→            if isinstance(timestamp, str) and timestamp.strip():
 270→                return timestamp
 271→    return None
 272→
 273→
 274→def _arrival_position(telemetry: Any) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
 275→    """The {lat, lng} of the telemetry row whose status is "arrived", or None.
 276→
 277→    None is a real answer — NS-0205's record has no arrival row, and that absence is the
 278→    evidence that escalates the case. Substituting the pickup point or the last row would
 279→    supply a position the record does not contain.
 280→    """
 281→    for row in telemetry if isinstance(telemetry, list) else []:
 282→        if isinstance(row, dict) and row.get("status") == "arrived":
 283→            lat, lng = row.get("lat"), row.get("lng")
 284→            if isinstance(lat, (int, float)) and isinstance(lng, (int, float)):
 285→                return {"lat": lat, "lng": lng}
 286→    return None
 287→
 288→
 289→def _organiser_profile(party: str, raw: Any) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
 290→    """One side's profile, in our field names. None when the record has no such block."""
 291→    profile = _object(raw)
 292→    if not profile:
 293→        return None
 294→    history = _object(profile.get("dispute_history"))
 295→    mapped: Dict[str, Any] = {}
 296→    _copy_present(mapped, profile, "%s_id" % party, "party_id")
 297→    _copy_present(mapped, profile, "account_age_days")
 298→    _copy_present(mapped, profile, "total_trips", "trips_completed")
 299→    _copy_present(mapped, profile, "avg_rating", "rating")
 300→    _copy_present(mapped, profile, "fraud_flags")
 301→    _copy_present(mapped, history, "total_disputes", "disputes_total")
 302→    # A rider's history counts disputes they won ("upheld"); a driver's counts disputes
 303→    # lost against them ("upheld_against"). Both land on disputes_upheld, which is the
 304→    # field the pack turns into the upheld rate the agents argue from.
 305→    _copy_present(mapped, history, "upheld_against" if party == "driver" else "upheld", "disputes_upheld")
 306→    return mapped
 307→
 308→
 309→def _organiser_to_record(data: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
 310→    """Translate one organisers'-shape record into our shape. See the module docstring."""
 311→    ticket = _object(data.get("dispute_ticket"))
 312→    trip_data = _object(data.get("trip_data"))
 313→    extensions = _object(data.get("ryde_extensions"))
 314→    category = normalise_category(ticket.get("dispute_type"))
 315→
 316→    # The claim and the intake answers live in our extension block; their own shape has no
 317→    # slot for either. Without the block (DISP-002) the description is all the party said,
 318→    # and no amount was asked for.
 319→    claim = extensions.get("claim")
 320→    if claim is None:
 321→        claim = {"text": ticket.get("description")}
 322→
 323→    trip: Dict[str, Any] = {}
 324→    for source, target in (
 325→        ("trip_id", "trip_id"),
 326→        ("rider_id", "rider_id"),
 327→        ("driver_id", "driver_id"),
 328→        ("estimated_duration_min", "estimated_duration_min"),
 329→        ("estimated_distance_km", "estimated_distance_km"),
 330→        ("requested_time", "requested_at"),
 331→        ("pickup_time", "pickup_at"),
 332→        ("dropoff_time", "dropoff_at"),
 333→    ):
 334→        _copy_present(trip, trip_data, source, target)
 335→    _copy_present(trip, extensions, "service_type")
 336→
 337→    if isinstance(trip_data.get("fare"), dict):
 338→        trip["fare"] = trip_data["fare"]
 339→    else:
 340→        # Their shape states a cancellation or waiting fee once, on trip_data; ours states
 341→        # it twice — on the cancellation block and as the charged amount in the fare
 342→        # breakdown. The reader places it in both, or the fee would vanish from the pack.
 343→        fee = trip_data.get("cancellation_fee")
 344→        if fee is None:
 345→            fee = trip_data.get("waiting_fee")
 346→        if fee is not None:
 347→            trip["fare"] = {"charged_sgd": fee, "breakdown": {"cancellation_sgd": fee}}
 348→
 349→    # Their gps_telemetry is the trip trace for a route case, but for a no-show it is the
 350→    # approach-and-wait trace: a route built from it would report a distance the trip never
 351→    # covered, so it becomes actual_route only where the trip actually ran.
 352→    if category == CATEGORY_ROUTE_DEVIATION:
 353→        route = [
 354→            {"lat": row.get("lat"), "lng": row.get("lng"), "t": row.get("timestamp")}
 355→            for row in (data.get("gps_telemetry") if isinstance(data.get("gps_telemetry"), list) else [])
 356→            if isinstance(row, dict)
 357→        ]
 358→        if route:
 359→            trip["actual_route"] = route
 360→
 361→    cancellation: Dict[str, Any] = {}
 362→    arrived_at = trip_data.get("driver_arrival_time")
 363→    wait_started_at = trip_data.get("driver_wait_start")
 364→    # A waiting fee is charged when the trip went ahead, so the boarding time is the
 365→    # moment the charge was incurred (NS-0207); otherwise it is the cancellation.
 366→    cancelled_at = trip_data.get("cancellation_time")
 367→    if cancelled_at is None:
 368→        cancelled_at = trip_data.get("rider_boarded_time")
 369→    fee = trip_data.get("cancellation_fee")
 370→    if fee is None:
 371→        fee = trip_data.get("waiting_fee")
 372→
 373→    has_cancellation_facts = any(
 374→        value is not None
 375→        for value in (
 376→            arrived_at,
 377→            wait_started_at,
 378→            cancelled_at,
 379→            fee,
 380→            trip_data.get("cancellation_reason"),
 381→        )
 382→    )
 383→    if has_cancellation_facts:
 384→        _copy_present(cancellation, trip_data, "driver_arrival_time", "driver_arrived_at")
 385→        _copy_present(cancellation, trip_data, "driver_wait_start", "wait_started_at")
 386→        if cancelled_at is not None:
 387→            cancellation["cancelled_at"] = cancelled_at
 388→        # Each fee is carried under its own name, so a record stating both loses
 389→        # neither (schema 1.3). cancellation_fee_sgd alone keeps the twin property:
 390→        # with no cancellation fee stated, the fee this reader places in the fare
 391→        # breakdown below (the waiting fee) stands in for comparison downstream.
 392→        if trip_data.get("cancellation_fee") is not None:
 393→            cancellation["cancellation_fee_sgd"] = trip_data["cancellation_fee"]
 394→        if trip_data.get("waiting_fee") is not None:
 395→            cancellation["waiting_fee_sgd"] = trip_data["waiting_fee"]
 396→        # Never the booking time: the pack's matching anchor names its source, and a proxy
 397→        # anchor invented here would be indistinguishable from a real one.
 398→        matched_at = _event_timestamp(data.get("app_events"), "driver_assigned")
 399→        if matched_at is not None:
 400→            cancellation["matched_at"] = matched_at
 401→        cancellation["driver_marked_no_show"] = trip_data.get("cancellation_reason") == "rider_no_show"
 402→        if "rider_claims_driver_absent" in extensions:
 403→            cancellation["rider_claims_driver_absent"] = extensions["rider_claims_driver_absent"]
 404→        # Never inferred: whether the rider says the driver never came is a structured
 405→        # fact only when the record states one (in ryde_extensions). Without it the field
 406→        # stays unset and the pack reports None — the rider's own words remain in
 407→        # claim.text, where the Advocates read them.
 408→        pickup = _object(trip_data.get("pickup_location"))
 409→        if "lat" in pickup and "lng" in pickup:
 410→            cancellation["pickup_point"] = {"lat": pickup.get("lat"), "lng": pickup.get("lng")}
 411→        position = _arrival_position(data.get("gps_telemetry"))
 412→        if position is not None:
 413→            cancellation["driver_gps_at_arrival"] = position
 414→        # The terms that govern this case, so the agents can see which policy the charge
 415→        # was applied under. Their shape carries it per case; passed through untouched.
 416→        if isinstance(data.get("cancellation_policy"), dict):
 417→            cancellation["case_policy"] = data["cancellation_policy"]
 418→
 419→    chat_log: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
 420→    for message in data.get("chat_logs") if isinstance(data.get("chat_logs"), list) else []:
 421→        if not isinstance(message, dict):
 422→            continue
 423→        entry: Dict[str, Any] = {
 424→            "t": message.get("timestamp"),
 425→            "sender": message.get("sender"),
 426→            "text": message.get("content"),
 427→        }
 428→        # A call is stronger evidence of a contact attempt than a message, and "type" is
 429→        # the only thing that tells them apart.
 430→        if "type" in message:
 431→            entry["type"] = message["type"]
 432→        chat_log.append(entry)
 433→
 434→    profiles: Dict[str, Any] = {}
 435→    for party in ("rider", "driver"):
 436→        profile = _organiser_profile(party, data.get("%s_profile" % party))
 437→        if profile is not None:
 438→            profiles[party] = profile
 439→
 440→    return {
 441→        "dispute_id": ticket.get("dispute_id"),
 442→        "category": ticket.get("dispute_type"),
 443→        "filed_by": ticket.get("filed_by"),
 444→        "filed_at": ticket.get("filed_at"),
 445→        "claim": claim,
 446→        "intake": extensions.get("intake") or {},
 447→        "trip": trip,
 448→        "cancellation": cancellation,
 449→        "chat_log": chat_log,
 450→        "profiles": profiles,
 451→        # Their shape has no slot for the party's round-two answers either; our
 452→        # extension block is the one place they can arrive.
 453→        "follow_up_answers": extensions.get("follow_up_answers"),
 454→    }
 455→
 456→
 457→# ------------------------------------------------------------- the shared parse
 458→
 459→
 460→def parse_dispute(data: Any) -> Dispute:
 461→    """Validate a raw dispute dict into a Dispute. Raises DisputeError with the reason."""
 462→    if not isinstance(data, dict):
 463→        raise DisputeError("a dispute record must be a JSON object")
 464→    # `raw` keeps the record exactly as it arrived, whichever shape that was: the case
 465→    # file's grievance section and the filed-dispute event show what was actually filed.
 466→    return _parse_record(_organiser_to_record(data) if is_organiser_record(data) else data, raw=data)
 467→
 468→
 469→def _follow_up_answers(value: Any) -> List[Dict[str, str]]:
 470→    """Validate the party's round-two answers, or [] when the record carries none.
 471→
 472→    Each entry must be an object with a string question and a string answer. Anything
 473→    else is a broken record: coercing it would put words in the party's mouth on the
 474→    file the advocates and the Judge read.
 475→    """
 476→    if value is None:
 477→        return []
 478→    if not isinstance(value, list):
 479→        raise DisputeError("follow_up_answers must be a list of {question, answer} objects")
 480→    answers: List[Dict[str, str]] = []
 481→    for item in value:
 482→        if not isinstance(item, dict):
 483→            raise DisputeError("follow_up_answers entries must be objects with question and answer")
 484→        question = item.get("question")
 485→        answer = item.get("answer")
 486→        if not isinstance(question, str) or not isinstance(answer, str):
 487→            raise DisputeError(
 488→                "follow_up_answers entries need a string 'question' and a string 'answer'"
 489→            )
 490→        answers.append({"question": question, "answer": answer})
 491→    return answers
 492→

 494→def _parse_record(data: Dict[str, Any], raw: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dispute:

1→"""The swappable policy document.
   2→
   3→Policy is data, not code: `docs/policy.md` is authored in another lane, carries its own
   4→provenance, and drops in without a code change. This module reads it, extracts the rule
   5→IDs agents must cite, and fails loudly when the file is missing — a run without policy is
   6→not a run this system is willing to make.
   7→
   8→Rule definition convention accepted by the loader (a line *begins* a rule when the rule
   9→ID is its first token, after any markdown decoration, and is not simply a wrapped
  10→sentence that happens to continue with the ID):
  11→
  12→    ### RD-1 — Route deviation threshold      heading style
  13→    **RD-1** Route deviation threshold        bold style
  14→    | RD-1 | Route deviation threshold | ...  table-row style
  15→
  16→A rule ID that appears mid-sentence is a cross-reference, not a definition, and is
  17→ignored. A line that starts with the ID but continues as prose ("ESC-4 cap, and
  18→applies to route cases only — ...", a wrapped sentence from the previous paragraph) is
  19→a cross-reference too, not a definition: real definitions are followed by a separator
  20→(em dash, closing bold, table pipe), never by a lowercase continuation word. If an ID
  21→is defined twice, the first definition wins.
  22→
  23→The loader exposes rule IDs and rule text. Evaluating the machine-checkable preconditions
  24→against an Evidence Pack is a later capability; nothing here interprets policy.
  25→"""
  26→
  27→from __future__ import annotations
  28→
  29→import re
  30→from dataclasses import dataclass
  31→from pathlib import Path
  32→from typing import Dict, Iterable, List, Optional
  33→
  34→#: Rule IDs look like RD-1, NS-2, GEN-1 — 2-5 capitals, a hyphen, a number.
  35→RULE_ID_PATTERN = re.compile(r"\b([A-Z]{2,5}-\d{1,3})\b")
  36→
  37→#: A line defines a rule only when its first token is the rule ID, followed by a
  38→#: separator rather than a continuation word (see the module docstring).
  39→_DEFINITION_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^[\s#*|>\-]*([A-Z]{2,5}-\d{1,3})\b(?!\s[a-z])")
  40→
  41→
  42→class PolicyError(RuntimeError):
  43→    """The policy document is missing, unreadable, or has no usable rules."""
  44→
  45→
  46→@dataclass(frozen=True)
  47→class PolicyRule:
  48→    """One rule, with the text that defines it."""
  49→
  50→    rule_id: str
  51→    text: str
  52→    line_number: int
  53→
  54→
  55→@dataclass(frozen=True)
  56→class PolicySet:
  57→    """The loaded policy document."""
  58→
  59→    source_path: Path
  60→    text: str
  61→    rules: List[PolicyRule]
  62→
  63→    def rule_ids(self) -> List[str]:
  64→        return [rule.rule_id for rule in self.rules]
  65→
  66→    def has_rule(self, rule_id: str) -> bool:
  67→        return any(rule.rule_id == rule_id for rule in self.rules)
  68→
  69→    def rule_text(self, rule_id: str) -> str:
  70→        for rule in self.rules:
  71→            if rule.rule_id == rule_id:
  72→                return rule.text
  73→        raise KeyError("no rule %r in %s" % (rule_id, self.source_path))
  74→
  75→    def rule_title(self, rule_id: str) -> str:
  76→        """The rule's plain heading title, for party-facing citations.
  77→
  78→        From the definition line's text after the em dash, with the rule ID and any
  79→        provenance tag `[...]` stripped: '### RD-1 — When a deviation is material
  80→        [SYNTHESISED]' -> 'When a deviation is material'. Raises KeyError for an
  81→        unknown ID, like rule_text.
  82→        """
  83→        text = self.rule_text(rule_id)
  84→        first_line = text.splitlines()[0] if text else ""
  85→        # Provenance tags first, so a tag containing the ID cannot confuse the next step.
  86→        line = re.sub(r"\[[^\]]*\]", "", first_line)
  87→        line = re.sub(r"^[#*\s|>\-]+", "", line)
  88→        line = re.sub(r"^%s\b" % re.escape(rule_id), "", line, count=1)
  89→        return line.lstrip("—–-:|* \t").strip()
  90→
  91→    def unknown_rule_ids(self, cited: Iterable[str]) -> List[str]:
  92→        """Which of the cited IDs are not in the document — i.e. invented by a model."""
  93→        known = set(self.rule_ids())
  94→        return [rule_id for rule_id in cited if rule_id not in known]
  95→
  96→
  97→def extract_rules(text: str) -> List[PolicyRule]:
  98→    """Split a policy document into rule blocks, in document order."""
  99→    rules: List[PolicyRule] = []
 100→    seen: Dict[str, PolicyRule] = {}
 101→    current: Optional[PolicyRule] = None
 102→    buffer: List[str] = []
 103→
 104→    def flush() -> None:
 105→        if current is not None and current.rule_id not in seen:
 106→            block = PolicyRule(current.rule_id, "\n".join(buffer).strip(), current.line_number)
 107→            seen[current.rule_id] = block
 108→            rules.append(block)
 109→
 110→    for line_number, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), start=1):
 111→        match = _DEFINITION_PATTERN.match(line)
 112→        if match:
 113→            flush()
 114→            current = PolicyRule(match.group(1), "", line_number)
 115→            buffer = [line]
 116→            continue
 117→        if current is not None:
 118→            buffer.append(line)
 119→
 120→    flush()
 121→    return rules
 122→
 123→
 124→def load_policy(path: Path) -> PolicySet:
 125→    """Load and validate the policy document. Raises PolicyError if it cannot be used."""
 126→    policy_path = Path(path)
 127→    if not policy_path.exists():
 128→        raise PolicyError(
 129→            "policy document not found at %s. The policy set is a required input: it is "
 130→            "authored separately and must land at that path before the pipeline can run. "
 131→            "Tests use the minimal fixture in tests/fixtures/ instead." % policy_path
 132→        )
 133→    if not policy_path.is_file():
 134→        raise PolicyError("policy path is not a file: %s" % policy_path)
 135→
 136→    text = policy_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
 137→    if not text.strip():
 138→        raise PolicyError("policy document is empty: %s" % policy_path)
 139→
 140→    rules = extract_rules(text)
 141→    if not rules:
 142→        raise PolicyError(
 143→            "no rules found in %s. Rules must be numbered IDs whose first token on a line "
 144→            "is the ID, e.g. '### RD-1 — Route deviation threshold'." % policy_path
 145→        )
 146→    return PolicySet(source_path=policy_path, text=text, rules=rules)
 147→

 184→def _diagram(text: str):
 185→    """(labels by lowercased label -> node id, set of (from_id, to_id) edges)."""
 186→    block = MERMAID.findall(text)[0]
 187→    labels = {}
 188→    for match in NODE_LABEL.finditer(block):
 189→        label = next(g for g in match.groups()[1:] if g)
 190→        labels.setdefault(label.strip().lower(), match.group(1))
 191→    edges = set()
 192→    for line in block.splitlines():
 193→        bare = BRACKETS.sub("", QUOTED.sub("", line))
 194→        found = EDGE.match(bare)
 195→        if found:
 196→            edges.add((found.group(1), found.group(2)))
 197→    return labels, edges

 200→def _node(labels, *needles):
 201→    for label, node_id in labels.items():
 202→        if all(n in label for n in needles):
 203→            return node_id
 204→    return None

1→# Architecture
   2→
   3→This document explains the system to someone who has read the README and has five minutes.
   4→Every claim here describes the code as it stands; nothing is planned or partial except where
   5→the Limits section says so plainly.
   6→
   7→## Overview
   8→
   9→Ryde is a multi-agent dispute resolution system for ride-hailing: a party files a dispute
  10→through a web intake form, and the system resolves the two categories it handles — route
  11→deviation and no-show charge — end to end. Three agents do the work: a Rider Advocate and a
  12→Driver Advocate each build their side's case from the evidence, and a Judge weighs both
  13→cases, applies company policy and issues a ruling with a confidence score. Every computed
  14→figure the agents argue from comes from a deterministic Evidence Pack calculated in Python
  15→before any model is called; agents cite pack fields by reference and are forbidden from
  16→doing their own arithmetic, and the only other number they see is the amount the party
  17→asked for. The decisions that must never depend on a model's obedience — the confidence
  18→threshold, the SGD 50 autonomous cap, the requirement that a route ruling rest on a measured
  19→deviation, the three money gates NS-6, RD-5 and RD-4, the one-round follow-up limit, and the routing of
  20→out-of-scope categories to human review — are enforced in Python code, not asked of the model in
  21→a prompt. The system
  22→has two surfaces: an operator console that shows the full case file and the agent-to-agent
  23→traffic, and a party page where the filing party submits the form and reads only what they
  24→are allowed to read.
  25→
  26→## Diagram
  27→
  28→The whole system on one page. A dispute arrives either through the web intake form or the
  29→command-line runner; the two swappable inputs (the policy document and the dataset pack)
  30→enter from the side. Every step of a run lands in the event log, and the operator console
  31→renders the event strip embedded in the case file — opening each event's full payload from
  32→the run files the operator attaches.
  33→
  34→```mermaid
  35→flowchart TD
  36→    PACK["Dataset pack"] --> B["Server"]
  37→    PACK --> CL["Command-line runner"]
  38→    A["Rider intake form"] --> B
  39→    B --> C{"Category in scope?"}
  40→    CL --> C
  41→    C -- "Out of scope" --> H["Human review"]
  42→    C -- "Route deviation or no-show" --> E["Evidence Pack"]
  43→    POL["Policy document"] --> RA["Rider Advocate"]
  44→    POL --> DA["Driver Advocate"]
  45→    POL --> J["Judge"]
  46→    E --> RA
  47→    E --> DA
  48→    RA --> S{"Questions for the party?"}
  49→    DA --> S
  50→    S -- "Yes, first round" --> O4["Needs info"]
  51→    O4 --> PA["Party answers follow-ups"]
  52→    PA -- "Fresh run with the answers" --> B
  53→    S -- "No" --> J
  54→    J --> G{"Gates pass? Confidence, cap, measured deviation, NS-6, RD-5, RD-4"}
  55→    G -- "Yes" --> O1["Ruled"]
  56→    G -- "No" --> O2["Withheld"]
  57→    O2 -- "Candidate ruling queued" --> H
  58→    J -- "Model could not answer" --> H
  59→    B -. "Every step emits an event" .-> L["Event log"]
  60→    J -.-> L
  61→    L -- "Embedded in the case file" --> K["Operator console"]
  62→```
  63→
  64→## Components
  65→
  66→| Component | File(s) | Responsibility |
  67→|---|---|---|
  68→| Pipeline | `app/pipeline.py` | Runs one dispute end to end, moves the case between agents, records every step |
  69→| Dispute record and routing | `app/dispute.py` | Parses the two record shapes, normalises categories, routes out-of-scope filings away |
  70→| Evidence layer | `app/evidence/compute.py` | Computes the Evidence Pack by plain arithmetic; a missing input inside a record becomes a null with a note, never a guess — a number that is present but **not a finite number** (NaN or Infinity, which a JSON reader accepts, or an **integer too large** for a float) counts as missing, and it voids what it feeds rather than being dropped from a formula. A figure the layer's own arithmetic would **overflow** into (a huge distance over a tiny estimate) is missing too, never Infinity. An **impossible** input — a negative rate, a surge of zero or less, or a promo larger than the fare — voids the fare the same way, with a note and an entry in `fare.unreadable_inputs`. A route case with no trip record, or a no-show case with no cancellation record, aborts the run before any pack is built |
  71→| Agent scaffolding | `app/agents/base.py` | Shared prompts, the LLM call, and citation validation against the pack and the policy |
  72→| Rider Advocate | `app/agents/rider_advocate.py` | Argues the rider's side from the pack and the policy |
  73→| Driver Advocate | `app/agents/driver_advocate.py` | Argues the driver's side from the pack and the policy |
  74→| Judge | `app/agents/judge.py` | Weighs both cases, issues one ruling, withholds it behind the gates |
  75→| Event log | `app/events.py` | The append-only record of who said what to whom, with full payloads on disk |
  76→| Output contracts | `app/schemas.py` | The typed shapes agents must produce; builds the party-facing decision message |
  77→| Policy loader | `app/policy.py` | Reads the policy document, extracts rule IDs, fails loudly when it is missing |
  78→| Mock LLM | `app/llm/mock.py` | Deterministic stand-in provider; its free-text fields — claim summaries, arguments, the Judge's explanation — carry a `MOCK` prefix, while actions, rule IDs and evidence refs do not |
  79→| Tencent adapter | `app/llm/tencent.py` | The real provider: calls one Tencent Cloud ADP app per agent over HTTP |
  80→| HTTP server | `app/server.py` | The intake API, the party view allowlist, and static files for both pages |
  81→| Command-line runner | `app/cli.py` | Runs one dispute from the terminal and prints the event strip |
  82→| Runtime configuration | `app/config.json` | Confidence threshold, autonomous cap, default dataset pack, provider settings |
  83→| Operator console | `ui/app.js` | Renders the case file: grievance, evidence, both claims, resolution, event strip |
  84→| Party page | `ui/party/party.js` | The intake form and the outcome view the filing party sees |
  85→| Policy document | `docs/policy.md` | The rule set the agents cite, with per-rule provenance |
  86→
  87→## Lifecycle of a dispute
  88→
  89→`run_dispute` in `app/pipeline.py` walks one dispute through these steps, in this order,
  90→emitting an event at each:
  91→
  92→1. `run.started` — the system records the dispute id, category, LLM provider, confidence
  93→   threshold and the policy rule IDs in force.
  94→2. `dispute.filed` — the raw intake-form submission is logged exactly as it arrived.
  95→3. **Routing.** If the category is outside the two handled ones, the run emits
  96→   `dispute.routed_to_human_review`, then `party.notified` with the neutral support message,
  97→   then `run.completed` — and no agent runs at all.
  98→4. `evidence.pack_built` — the Evidence Pack is computed in Python, before any LLM call,
  99→   and offered to the agents as the source of every computed figure — the only other
 100→   number they see is the amount the party claimed.
 101→5. `case.assigned` — once to each advocate.
 102→6. Each advocate runs and emits `advocate.case_submitted` to the Judge with its case. When
 103→   an advocate needs more from the filing party, it selects offered slot IDs and emits
 104→   `advocate.follow_up_requested` in the first round with both the selected slots and the
 105→   rendered questions. Code renders a bank sentence for a rider-filed dispute, or a form
 106→   sentence from an intake label for either filer; any question text written by the model
 107→   is ignored. The party-safety check remains a backstop, and only rendered questions that
 108→   pass it reach the party.
 109→7. **Stop and ask.** If there are questions to send and the dispute does not already carry
 110→   the party's answers, the run stops before the Judge: `party.notified` carries the
 111→   rendered questions — or, when none survive the backstop, plain template questions the
 112→   pipeline builds for blank intake fields — then `run.completed` records the `needs_info`
 113→   outcome. The party's answers start a fresh run, which is guaranteed to reach the Judge.
 114→8. `judge.deliberation_started` — both cases are handed to the Judge together.
 115→9. The Judge rules: `judge.ruling_issued` when every gate passes, or
 116→   `judge.ruling_withheld` when one fails — the candidate ruling is recorded either way.
 117→10. `party.notified` — the message the parties actually receive, as opposed to what was
 118→    decided internally.
 119→11. `run.completed` — the outcome is recorded and the case file is written.
 120→
 121→## The four outcomes
 122→
 123→| Outcome | When it happens | Did the Judge run? | Party page shows |
 124→|---|---|---|---|
 125→| `ruled` | The Judge issued a ruling and every gate passed | Yes | `decided` |
 126→| `withheld` | A gate stopped the ruling, or the model could not answer after its allowed retries | Yes for a gate — the candidate is recorded for a human reviewer, never delivered; no candidate exists for a model failure | `under_review` |
 127→| `human_review` | The category is outside the two the agents handle | No — routed away before any agent | `passed_to_support` |
 128→| `needs_info` | The advocates selected offered follow-up slots in the first round, or a blank form answer produced a template question | No — the run stops before the Judge | `needs_info` |
 129→
 130→## Gates enforced in code
 131→
 132→Nine gates stand between a filing and a ruling, and each is enforced in Python, not asked of
 133→the model in a prompt:
 134→
 135→| Gate | File | Condition as written in code |
 136→|---|---|---|
 137→| Confidence threshold | `app/agents/judge.py` | `ruling.confidence < confidence_threshold` — the threshold is 0.65, read from `app/config.json` |
 138→| ESC-4, the autonomous cap | `app/agents/judge.py` | A money ruling whose `recommended_amount_sgd` exceeds the cap is withheld; the cap is SGD 50 from `app/config.json` |
 139→| ESC-2, unmeasured deviation, unproven charge or unreadable fare input | `app/agents/judge.py` | On a route-deviation case, the ruling is withheld when `route.deviation_pct` is not a recorded finite figure, when `fare.charged_sgd` is not one (or the fare block is absent), or when the record states a fare input it cannot read (`fare.unreadable_inputs` non-empty: a broken tariff rate or promo) — EV-1 names the deviation and the fare charged as the figures a fare finding needs, and a figure the record cannot prove is a missing figure |
 140→| NS-6, contested no-show | `app/agents/judge.py` | On a no-show case where the driver marked a no-show, the rider claims the driver was absent, and `cancellation.driver_distance_from_pickup_m` is null, the fee has no GPS proof: a refund is issued automatically only when the fee is at most SGD 10 and the rider's `fraud_flags` are recorded and zero with no more than half of past disputes rejected; any other ruling is withheld, and the refund must equal the fee to the cent |
 141→| RD-5, proven overcharge | `app/agents/judge.py` | On a route-deviation case where `fare.difference_sgd` is recorded and at least SGD 1.00, a ruling that refunds less than the proven difference is withheld |
 142→| RD-4, unproven refund | `app/agents/judge.py` | On a route-deviation case, a refund larger than the records prove the rider overpaid is withheld — the proof is the largest of a positive `fare.difference_sgd`, the charge above an inconsistent breakdown total (EV-3, no rates needed), and, only for a material deviation under RD-1, the charge above `fare.recomputed_estimated_route_sgd` — and a `compensation` ruling is always withheld, because a route record proves nothing owed to the driver |
 143→| One-round follow-up limit | `app/pipeline.py` | `if questions and not dispute.follow_up_answers` — a dispute is asked at most once; with answers present the Judge always runs and fresh questions are recorded but not sent |
 144→| Out-of-scope routing | `app/pipeline.py` | `if not dispute.is_agent_handled` — anything outside route deviation and no-show charge goes to human review before any agent runs; an unrecognised category normalises to "other" in `app/dispute.py` |
 145→| Answer once | `app/server.py` | The answers route claims the run with an exclusive create (`O_CREAT \| O_EXCL`) before re-running it — a `needs_info` run can be answered exactly once and cannot produce two rulings |
 146→
 147→Why in code? Because a prompt is a request — a model can misread it, and there is no
 148→recourse when it does. Code is a guarantee: the branch either runs or it does not, and the
 149→event log shows which. ESC-4 in particular moves money, so it must not depend on the LLM
 150→having read its instructions carefully.
 151→
 152→## Observability
 153→
 154→Every run writes three things under `runs/<run_id>/`:
 155→
 156→- `events.jsonl` — one JSON line per event, append-only, never rewritten: who sent what to
 157→  whom, when, with a one-line summary.
 158→- `payloads/` — the full payload behind each event, named by sequence number and event
 159→  type, so the strip stays readable and the detail stays one click away.
 160→- `case_file.json` — the assembled record: what was claimed, the evidence pack, both
 161→  advocate cases, the resolution, and the event strip. Self-contained, so one file tells
 162→  the whole story of one run.
 163→
 164→A run filed through the server writes one more file: `dispute.json`, the record the pipeline
 165→actually ran on (the command-line runner does not write it). When a `needs_info` run is
 166→answered, its directory also gains `answered.json`, recording which run the answers
 167→produced.
 168→
 169→The operator console (`ui/app.js`) renders the case file: the event strip shows one row per
 170→event — sequence, time, sender to recipient, summary — and expanding a row opens the full
 171→payload from the run directory attached in the browser. Payload references are sanitised, so
 172→a console loaded with a hostile file can be pointed at nothing outside the run. The
 173→command-line runner prints the same strip to the terminal.
 174→
 175→## What the parties see
 176→
 177→`party_view` in `app/server.py` is an allowlist that fails closed. The party page is handed
 178→exactly five keys — run id, dispute id, status, message, questions — and any malformed case
 179→file degrades to the neutral under-review message with no questions. A withheld ruling's
 180→amount and the Judge's confidence are structurally absent from everything the party is
 181→sent, not merely unrendered. `party_message_for_ruling` in `app/schemas.py` composes the
 182→decision message in code from structured fields — the action, the amount, and the plain
 183→titles of the policy rules cited — and the Judge's explanation never crosses this boundary:
 184→it stays in the operator console. Every non-decision status shows a canonical constant
 185→message, whatever a stale or planted case file might say. The two kinds of party-facing text
 186→are protected differently. The decision message is composed in code from structured fields,
 187→so nothing model-written reaches it: it names the action and the amount — a no-action ruling
 188→carries no amount — and at most three rule titles, never the escalation (ESC) rules. On a
 189→decided view the message leads with a demo notice whenever the ruling's LLM record does not
 190→prove the real provider — only a record that is a non-array dict whose provider field is
 191→exactly `tencent` suppresses it, and any other record, missing, mock or malformed, keeps it —
 192→so a decision made on an illustrative run never reads like a live review, while a proven
 193→real-provider decision shows no notice.
 194→Follow-up questions are selected by the advocates as slot IDs; code renders each sentence
 195→from the fixed category bank or from an intake form label. Bank slots are offered only when
 196→the rider filed, while form slots work for either filer. Any question text written by the
 197→model is ignored, so no model-written text reaches a party. The word check (`is_party_safe`,
 198→applied in `_questions_for_party` in `app/pipeline.py` and again in `party_view`) remains a
 199→backstop, as it is for the code-composed decision message. When no rendered question survives,
 200→the pipeline falls back to plain template questions built from the form's own labels. A run
 201→that asked for more information is answered through `POST /api/disputes/<run_id>/answers`, and
 202→the answers start a fresh run on the same dispute.
 203→
 204→## Policy and dataset packs
 205→
 206→`docs/policy.md` is data, not code: rules with IDs (GEN, EV, RD, NS, ESC families),
 207→preconditions written against pack fields in plain language, and per-rule provenance
 208→stating whether a rule comes from Ryde's own published policy, a comparable operator, or
 209→the project team. The pipeline reads it at the path in `app/config.json`; a different
 210→policy document drops in with no code change. Nothing in the code evaluates the
 211→preconditions — the Judge reads the rules and applies them in its reasoning. Citing a rule
 212→that does not exist is recorded rather than blocked: an unknown ID is logged under the
 213→ruling's `validation.unknown_rule_ids` with a note and the ruling still issues, but only
 214→titles of rules the policy actually defines can reach the party message.
 215→
 216→Two dataset packs live under `data/packs/`: `organiser-style-v1` — the default in
 217→`app/config.json` — which holds the corpus in the organisers' record shape, including their
 218→own DISP-002 verbatim; and `ryde-synth-v1`, the same 17 cases in this project's own record
 219→shape. Swapping corpora is a directory copy, never a code change. Each pack carries a
 220→`ground-truth.json` of expected outcomes, kept out of what the agents see: the agents get
 221→the dispute record, the evidence pack and the policy — never the answer — so replayed-run
 222→consistency can be measured honestly.
 223→
 224→## LLM provider
 225→
 226→Agent logic never talks to a vendor SDK. Every agent builds a request and calls one seam:
 227→the `LLMClient` interface in `app/llm/`, a single `complete` method whose response carries
 228→the text plus provenance (provider, model, usage, finish reason). Two adapters implement
 229→it. The mock provider, `app/llm/mock.py`, returns deterministic contract-shaped responses,
 230→so the full pipeline runs with no API key and the same dispute always produces the same
 231→decisions and the same computed figures (the run id and the event timestamps differ from
 232→run to run). Its free-text fields — claim summaries, arguments, the Judge's explanation —
 233→carry a `MOCK` prefix, so a mock run can never be mistaken for a real ruling; actions, rule
 234→IDs and evidence refs are not prefixed. The party decision message, composed in code, is
 235→marked differently: on a decided party view it leads with a fixed demo notice stating that
 236→the decision came from an illustrative run and is not a live review, shown whenever the
 237→ruling's LLM record does not prove the Tencent provider, and only a record whose provider
 238→field is exactly `tencent` shows a decision with no notice. The Tencent adapter,
 239→`app/llm/tencent.py`, implements the same interface over Tencent Cloud ADP (Agent
 240→Development Platform). Each agent is its own published ADP app with its own key: Rider
 241→Advocate, Driver Advocate and Judge. The apps carry only a short role card; the adapter
 242→sends the full role prompt on every call, so the prompts live in this repo and every gate
 243→stays in Python. Three things about the endpoint shape the adapter. Tencent's web firewall
 244→blocks prompts that mix backticks with ASCII brackets, so the adapter drops backticks and
 245→sends full-width brackets, which the model reads the same way; a blocked call is classified
 246→as permanent and is never asked again. ADP reports errors inside a successful HTTP response,
 247→so the adapter reads every event rather than trusting the status code. The free plan allows
 248→10 calls a minute, so calls are spaced at least 6.5 seconds apart. The agent layer retries a
 249→transient failure up to three times, with waits of 2, 5 and 10 seconds; a contract failure
 250→is asked again once. A parsed reply is final: a low confidence or capped ruling is never
 251→asked again. One case shares a 120 seconds time budget from `llm.case_budget_seconds`; each
 252→retry is recorded as `llm.call_retried`. When the budget cannot cover a call or wait, or the
 253→model still cannot answer, the pipeline returns a withheld case and emits
 254→`dispute.escalated_on_model_failure`; the case file keeps the `model_failure` record for the
 255→reviewer. There is no silent fallback to the mock. The mock stays the default provider, so
 256→the tests and a fresh checkout need no keys; `--llm tencent` selects the real model.
 257→
 258→## Limits
 259→
 260→What the system does not do yet, stated plainly:
 261→
 262→- **A failed model call is escalated.** The party waits while retries run and sees the neutral
 263→  under-review message; after the case is queued for human review, the party is not notified later.
 264→- **Amounts must come back as JSON numbers.** A model reply carrying an amount as a string
 265→  is rejected, never converted, because the value moves money.
 266→- **Two categories only.** Route deviation and no-show charge. Property damage and safety
 267→  incidents route to human review by design.
 268→- **The driver-side form is not built.** The party page files as the rider only; the
 269→  pipeline itself accepts driver-filed disputes, but no web form offers it yet.
 270→- **Follow-up wording is code-owned.** Advocates select slot IDs; code renders each question
 271→  from the fixed category bank or an intake form label, and model-written question text is
 272→  ignored. Bank slots are rider-only; form slots are available to either filer.
 273→- **The word check is a backstop.** Rendered follow-up questions and the code-composed decision
 274→  message pass the keyword gate, which is not a semantic guarantee; blank fields still use
 275→  template questions built from the form's own labels.
 276→- **Policy preconditions are not evaluated by code.** The rules are written against pack
 277→  fields in plain language; nothing checks them mechanically, and the Judge applies them by
 278→  reading them.
 279→

A case the Judge withheld — a gate stopped it, or the model could not answer — waits
for a person. This module owns every rule of that decision: what a valid body is, the
SGD 500 ceiling, the decide-once write, and the words the party eventually reads. The
server only routes HTTP; the pages only render.

The decision is stored as `human_decision.json` in the run directory, written
atomically (a temp file linked into place) so exactly one of N concurrent requests
wins. The run's other files are never rewritten: `case_file.json` and `dispute.json`
stay byte-identical, the existing lines of `events.jsonl` stay byte-identical, and one
`human.decision_recorded` event is appended. If that append fails the decision still
stands and the failure is logged.

No money gate is consulted again (operator ruling): the gate that held the case does
not hold the person. A change to SGD 55.16 on a case held by ESC-4 is accepted, and a
change to SGD 5.56 on a case held by RD-4 is accepted.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import math
import os
import sys
import tempfile
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict, Optional, Tuple

from . import events
from .events import Actor, EventType
from .schemas import (
    ContractError,
    OUTCOME_WITHHELD,
    RulingAction,
    _cited_rule_titles,
)

HUMAN_DECISION_FILE_NAME = "human_decision.json"
HUMAN_AMOUNT_CEILING_SGD = 500.0
HUMAN_REVIEWED_SENTENCE = "A member of our team reviewed your case."
DECISIONS = ("approve", "change", "reject")
REVIEWER_MAX_CHARS = 80
REASON_MAX_CHARS = 1000

NOT_WAITING_MESSAGE = "this case is not waiting for a human decision"
APPROVE_NO_EXTRAS_MESSAGE = "approve takes no action or amount; use change"
NO_PROPOSAL_MESSAGE = "there is no proposed ruling to approve"
ABOVE_CEILING_MESSAGE = "the proposed amount is above SGD 500.00; use change"
ALREADY_DECIDED_MESSAGE = "this case already has a human decision"


class HumanDecisionError(Exception):
    """A human decision the system refuses, with the HTTP status it maps to."""

    def __init__(self, status: int, message: str):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.status = status
        self.message = message


# --------------------------------------------------------------------- shape checks


def _finite_number(value: Any) -> Optional[float]:
    """The value as a finite float, or None. Bools and huge JSON ints are not figures."""
    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
        return None
    try:
        number = float(value)
    except OverflowError:  # a JSON int too large for a float is not a figure
        return None
    return number if math.isfinite(number) else None


def _valid_candidate(candidate: Any) -> Optional[Tuple[str, float]]:
    """(wire action, cent-rounded amount) for a usable withheld candidate, else None.

    The candidate is the Judge's proposal kept on the case file for the reviewer. A
    model failure leaves it None; a hand-edited or stale file may hold any shape, and
    anything that is not an action plus a finite figure is not something to approve.
    """
    if not isinstance(candidate, dict):
        return None
    try:
        action = RulingAction.parse(candidate.get("action"))
    except ContractError:
        return None
    amount = _finite_number(candidate.get("recommended_amount_sgd"))
    if amount is None:
        return None
    return action.value, round(amount, 2)


def decision_record_is_valid(value: Any) -> bool:
    """True for the record shape `load_decision` accepts: an action and a finite amount.

    A record that fails this is ignored, never partially trusted: the party view
    stays under review and the case stays in the queue.
    """
    if not isinstance(value, dict):
        return False
    if value.get("action") not in {member.value for member in RulingAction}:
        return False
    return _finite_number(value.get("amount_sgd")) is not None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------- validation


def validate_decision(body: Any, case_file: Any) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Validate one human decision against its case file. Pure — nothing touches disk.

    Raises HumanDecisionError with the HTTP status and the message the server relays.
    The order is fixed: the case must be waiting, then the decision, then the reviewer
    and the reason, then the decision's own fields.
    """
    resolution = case_file.get("resolution") if isinstance(case_file, dict) else None
    if not isinstance(resolution, dict) or resolution.get("outcome") != OUTCOME_WITHHELD:
        raise HumanDecisionError(409, NOT_WAITING_MESSAGE)
    if not isinstance(body, dict):
        raise HumanDecisionError(400, "the request body must be a JSON object")

    decision = body.get("decision")
    if not isinstance(decision, str) or decision not in DECISIONS:
        raise HumanDecisionError(400, "decision must be one of approve, change or reject")

    reviewer = body.get("reviewer")
    if not isinstance(reviewer, str):
        raise HumanDecisionError(400, "reviewer is required and must be a string")
    reviewer = reviewer.strip()
    if not reviewer:
        raise HumanDecisionError(400, "reviewer is required")
    if len(reviewer) > REVIEWER_MAX_CHARS:
        raise HumanDecisionError(400, "reviewer must be at most %d characters" % REVIEWER_MAX_CHARS)

    reason = body.get("reason")
    if not isinstance(reason, str):
        raise HumanDecisionError(400, "reason is required and must be a string")
    reason = reason.strip()
    if not reason:
        raise HumanDecisionError(400, "reason is required")
    if len(reason) > REASON_MAX_CHARS:
        raise HumanDecisionError(400, "reason must be at most %d characters" % REASON_MAX_CHARS)

    candidate = _valid_candidate(resolution.get("withheld_candidate"))
    proposed = None if candidate is None else {"action": candidate[0], "amount_sgd": candidate[1]}

    if decision == "approve":
        if "action" in body or "amount_sgd" in body:
            raise HumanDecisionError(400, APPROVE_NO_EXTRAS_MESSAGE)
        if candidate is None:
            raise HumanDecisionError(409, NO_PROPOSAL_MESSAGE)
        action, amount = candidate
        if action == RulingAction.NO_ACTION.value:
            amount = 0.0
        # The ceiling covers the proposal too: the model's amount has no upper bound in
        # its contract, so one click on a held SGD 600 proposal must not pay it.
        if amount > HUMAN_AMOUNT_CEILING_SGD:
            raise HumanDecisionError(400, ABOVE_CEILING_MESSAGE)
    elif decision == "change":
        try:
            parsed = RulingAction.parse(body.get("action"))
        except ContractError:
            raise HumanDecisionError(400, "action must be refund, compensation or no action")
        amount = _finite_number(body.get("amount_sgd"))
        if amount is None:
            raise HumanDecisionError(400, "amount_sgd must be a finite number")
        amount = round(amount, 2)
        if parsed is RulingAction.NO_ACTION:
            if amount != 0.0:
                raise HumanDecisionError(400, "a no-action decision carries no amount")
        elif amount <= 0.0:
            raise HumanDecisionError(400, "the amount must be above SGD 0.00")
        elif amount > HUMAN_AMOUNT_CEILING_SGD:
            raise HumanDecisionError(400, "the amount must be at most SGD 500.00")
        action = parsed.value
    else:  # reject
        if "action" in body or "amount_sgd" in body:
            raise HumanDecisionError(400, "reject takes no action or amount")
        action, amount = RulingAction.NO_ACTION.value, 0.0

    return {
        "schema_version": "1.0",
        "run_id": case_file.get("run_id"),
        "dispute_id": case_file.get("dispute_id"),
        "decision": decision,
        "reviewer": reviewer,
        "reason": reason,
        "action": action,
        "amount_sgd": amount,
        "proposed": proposed,
        "decided_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
    }


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------- storage


def record_decision(run_dir: Path, case_file: Any, body: Any) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Validate, then store the decision exactly once and append one event.

    Decide once, atomically: the record is written to a temp file in the run directory
    and hard-linked into place, so of N concurrent requests exactly one wins and the
    file is never empty or partial. A second sequential decision is refused. The
    append-only event is best-effort: if it fails the decision stands, the failure is
    logged to stderr, and the record is still returned.
    """
    record = validate_decision(body, case_file)
    run_dir = Path(run_dir)
    final_path = run_dir / HUMAN_DECISION_FILE_NAME

    handle, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".human-decision-", suffix=".tmp", dir=str(run_dir))
    tmp_path = Path(tmp_name)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(handle, "w", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
            stream.write(json.dumps(record, indent=2, sort_keys=False, default=str) + "\n")
        try:
            os.link(str(tmp_path), str(final_path))
        except FileExistsError:
            raise HumanDecisionError(409, ALREADY_DECIDED_MESSAGE)
    finally:
        try:
            tmp_path.unlink()
        except OSError:
            pass

    try:
        # Looked up through the module, so a test can patch app.events.append_event.
        events.append_event(
            run_dir,
            record["run_id"],
            EventType.HUMAN_DECISION_RECORDED,
            from_=Actor.HUMAN_REVIEW,
            to=Actor.PARTIES,
            summary="human reviewer %s decided: %s" % (record["reviewer"], record["decision"]),
            payload=record,
        )
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - the decision stands without the log line
        print(
            "human decision event append failed for run %s: %s" % (record["run_id"], exc),
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
    return record


def load_decision(run_dir: Path) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """The stored decision record, or None. Fails closed on any bad shape or file."""
    path = Path(run_dir) / HUMAN_DECISION_FILE_NAME
    try:
        data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return None
    return data if decision_record_is_valid(data) else None


# -------------------------------------------------------------------- party message


class _CandidateRules:
    """The one field `_cited_rule_titles` reads, so its exact rules are reused."""

    def __init__(self, cited_rule_ids):
        self.cited_rule_ids = cited_rule_ids


def _candidate_titles(withheld_candidate: Any, policy: Any) -> list:
    if policy is None or not isinstance(withheld_candidate, dict):
        return []
    cited = withheld_candidate.get("cited_rule_ids")
    if not isinstance(cited, list):
        return []
    return _cited_rule_titles(_CandidateRules([rid for rid in cited if isinstance(rid, str)]), policy)


def party_message_for_human_decision(record: Dict[str, Any], withheld_candidate: Any, policy: Any) -> str:
    """The party-facing text for a human decision (operator ruling 2026-10-03).

    An approval keeps the AI's Basis line, because the human accepted the proposal and
    its reasoning; a change or a rejection never carries one, because the citations may
    contradict what the person decided. The reviewer's name and reason never appear.
    """
    action = record.get("action") if isinstance(record, dict) else None
    amount = record.get("amount_sgd") if isinstance(record, dict) else None
    decision = record.get("decision") if isinstance(record, dict) else None

    if action == RulingAction.NO_ACTION.value:
        message = "Decision: no action."
    else:
        message = "Decision: %s of SGD %.2f." % (action, amount)
    if decision == "approve":
        titles = _candidate_titles(withheld_candidate, policy)
        if titles:
            message += " Basis: %s." % "; ".join(titles)
    return "%s %s" % (message, HUMAN_REVIEWED_SENTENCE)
"}

## Human decision

A case the Judge withholds — a gate stopped the ruling, or the model could not answer — waits
for a person; `app/human_review.py` owns that decision. The reviewer's action is validated in
code and stored as `human_decision.json` in the run directory, written atomically (a temp file
linked into place) so exactly one of several concurrent requests can decide and a second is
refused. The ceiling is SGD 500: the model's proposed amount has no upper bound, so an approval
above it is refused and the reviewer must use a change instead. No money gate is consulted
again — the gate that held the case does not hold the person — and `case_file.json` and
`dispute.json` are never rewritten. One `human.decision_recorded` event is appended to the
run's log; if that append fails the decision still stands. The party message is built in code:
an approval keeps the proposal's Basis line (the plain titles of the cited rules, escalation
rules excluded), while a change or a rejection never carries one, because the citations may
contradict the person's decision. The reviewer's name and reason never reach a party.

The server exposes the loop as JSON, all `Cache-Control: no-store`:

| Endpoint | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/review/<run_id>/decision` | Store one human decision on a withheld run (works for command-line runs too) |
| `GET /api/review/queue` | Every withheld run with no valid decision, safety cases first, then largest amount, longest wait |
| `GET /api/review/overrides` | Approvals counted; changes and rejections grouped by the shape of the departure |
| `GET /api/disputes/<dispute_id>` | The party's own view of their dispute's current run, with its decision applied |
| `GET /api/demo/rider` | The demo rider account: every dispute filed on this demo |
| `GET /api/demo/driver` | The demo driver account: read-only outcomes for the demo driver's trips |

Only direct children of the output folder that hold a case file are runs — eval runs live a
level deeper and are never seen — and a dispute's current run is the party-filed run without
`answered.json`, latest `generated_at` first. The pages are clients: `ui/party/status.html`
